title: Tide and Harbor
premise: Silas Dunmore, a cellist whose career ended in a humiliating collapse on a Boston stage, retreats to the coastal town of Harbor Light, where she has spent ten years writing anonymous letters to a wrongfully imprisoned man, Jonah Reyes—letters that kept him sane and gave her penance for the testimony she failed to give. When Jonah is finally exonerated and moves into the cottage next door, Silas must decide whether to confess that she was the girl who watched the crime, stayed silent, and built a life on that silence. As their friendship deepens into love, the truth threatens to destroy it, and Silas must choose between protecting her fragile new happiness and giving Jonah the justice the law never did. In the end, she speaks the rehearsed sentence—her public confession reopens the case against the real perpetrator—and Jonah, furious and grieving, must decide whether the letters and the liar were ever two different people, choosing her not because the past was forgivable but because she made the future true.
about_author: Sable Sandoval is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent years cataloging letters in coastal historical societies before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted boathouse in New England, where the tide sets her writing schedule.
